about: The shell conformance suite (docs/shell-interface.md section 16; N2 slice 4, halves since N3 slice 1). Each case runs on a new graph through any shell's control dispatcher: plumcraft_editor_core::conformance is the runner and says what a step is. Points are aimed with $locate, so a case holds whatever sizes the shell measured. half: read (changes nothing of the graph after its setup) or edit; needs: what a driver must have to run it.

cases.name: a shell's measurements are what the core hits
cases.about: geometry reported (typed on the C ABI, measured by egui) is what geometry.locate, geometry.hit and the scene use

cases.name: a tap selects; Shift adds; primary takes away; empty canvas clears
cases.about: selection.set by the egui canvas's click rules, decided in the core from the hit

cases.name: a tap on a pin or a wire watches its value
cases.about: run.watch of an output, of a wired input's source, of a wire's source; a wire's tap clears the selection as empty canvas does

cases.name: a drag moves an unselected face alone and leaves the selection
cases.about: drag begin decides a move of the face under it; move changes nothing; end is one edit.move by the offset, one undo step named for what moved, which one edit.undo takes back

cases.name: a drag on a selected face moves the selection
cases.about: every selected face moves by the same offset, in one edit.move: one undo step

cases.name: a cancelled drag leaves the document as it was
cases.about: begin and move change nothing; cancel forgets the drag; an end after it is an error

cases.name: a wire dragged from an output to an input is one undo step
cases.about: the target fits while it is dragged (JSON and typed); the drop is wire.connect; one edit.undo takes it away

cases.name: a new wire dropped on nothing opens the palette for what takes it; dismissing leaves nothing
cases.about: question 8: the drop is canvas.palette with the wire; the scene's view has it; palette.items offers only kinds with a port that takes it; closing it changes nothing

cases.name: a kind chosen from a dropped wire's palette is added with the wire, as one undo step
cases.about: question 8: palette.choose adds the node where the wire was dropped and connects it (node.addWired); one edit.undo takes both away; from an input the new node's output feeds it

cases.name: two drags are two undo steps; a held arrow key is one
cases.about: decision 3: each drag is one step, named by its serial, so the next drag of the same face is another; nudges naming one key press (drag) are one step

cases.name: a drop where a wire doesn't fit is refused with the reason
cases.about: a cycle: the target says fits 0 while dragged; the drop's wire.connect is refused and the graph keeps its wires

cases.name: a wire's end picked up off an input is rerouted, or dropped
cases.about: a drag on a wired input picks its wire's end up: onto another input it is wire.reroute, onto nothing wire.disconnect

cases.name: a marquee selects what it touches
cases.about: one-shot and dragged marquees: plain replaces, Shift adds, primary takes away

cases.name: a double tap opens what it is on
cases.about: a node's parameters, a wire's value popped out, the palette on empty canvas

cases.name: a context gesture gives the menu of what it is on
cases.about: a secondary click or long press: the menu model for a node, an input, an output, a wire; the palette on empty canvas

cases.name: a wire's right angles: drag an automatic corner, Make Right-Angled, Route Automatically
cases.about: B155: a wire running right to left is routed round its faces; a press on a corner of that route is a wire hit with part corner, and a drag there is a route drag ending in one wire.route that makes the route's corners the wire's own bend points (one undo step). wire.square (Make Right-Angled) gives a wire with no bend points its automatic route's corners; the wire's menu offers Route Automatically (wire.route {via: []}) once it has bend points

cases.name: a collapsed group's face is its group
cases.about: a tap selects the group, a drag moves it (one edit.move, members with it), a double tap enters it

cases.name: a frame is moved by its tab and sized by its handle
cases.about: frame.move and frame.resize at a drag's end, each one undo step

cases.name: a bend point is dragged, and removed by a double tap
cases.about: wire.route with the point moved; wire.route without it

cases.name: the scene's colours are tokens alone or colours alone, and theme.get has every token
cases.about: question 13, decided 13A: a token by name, a computed colour as [r, g, b, a]

cases.name: no two items of a scene share a nid
cases.about: faces, wires, nets, frames and groups are numbered from one counter a document

cases.name: the audio engine compiled in runs a tone through a gain to its peak and loudness
cases.about: 2026-11-21, "Compile array,audio,text in": a driver whose core has the audio engine compiled in (the C ABI's, so every native app) claims engine:audio; adding an audio node starts the audio engine in process (decision 8C); watching the peak runs the tone, the gain and the peak (a scalar), and a run of the whole graph the loudness too

cases.name: the engine's run as the faces show it: queued, progress, error, skipped, done, its time and its text
cases.about: The engine half in process (2026-11-22, the maintainer's "Compile array,audio,text in": the iPad's engine half uses the engines compiled in). The text engine's testing kinds, added by id (the palette doesn't offer them): text.slow reports progress in steps, text.fail always fails. Run: the faces the engine hasn't reached are queued at once (F31); the slow node's face shows its progress as the engine streams it (F38, F39); the failing node's face its error from the engine (F34), the node after it skipped (F39); the result's text is on its face (F46), the slow node's time in its header's status (F42); the run has an id and the generation rose (F28)

cases.name: the engine's run changed while it goes: stale, cancel, latest wins, a partial re-run, auto-run
cases.about: The engine half in process (2026-11-22). After a run, an edit upstream marks what it feeds stale and runs nothing (F45); run.cancel while the slow node works cancels it at once, and nothing after it is done (F36, F39 cancelled); a run started over one under way supersedes it, and the faces show the last edit's result (F29); a change after the slow node runs only what it touches, the slow node cached (F72, F39 cached); with auto-run on an edit runs by itself (F30). The slow node takes 0.9 s: under the second a result needs before it is persisted, so no store keeps one from an earlier launch (the iPad's store outlives a run, and a kept result made the first face done at once)

cases.name: ports: a variadic input, a choice's sub-port, and a choice this machine can't take
cases.about: The test engine `ports` (crates/ports, 2026-11-22): a driver with it (installed from a scratch engines folder as a process, or linked) claims engine:ports; one whose engine is installed but not started also claims ports_installed, and the case starts it first. A variadic input shows its slots (c1, c2) and the face its value joined from both (F14); the `line` choice brings its sub-port how.width, which the engine honours, and `space` takes it away (F15); a choice the engine says this machine can't take is offered disabled with its reason (F18)

cases.name: ports: a list, a wire's slice of it, and a path input
cases.about: The test engine `ports` (2026-11-22). A list output and a list input are marked as lists on the faces and a run counts the items (F20); a wire's slice `:-1` keeps a list one shorter and `-1` (an index) is refused into a list input and takes the last item alone into a single one, and the scene's wire says the slice (F21); a path input's widget is a path one opens, and run with none chosen it fails with the engine's reason (F16)

cases.name: ports: a setting bound to a bundle, and external ports on a collapsed group
cases.about: The test engine `ports` (2026-11-22). A port bound to a setting (`param_ref`, the node's `bundle_port`) takes its face's value until a bundle is wired in, whose value then wins (F13); a node's ports marked external are the collapsed group's own (F17)

cases.name: ports: Save Result writes a result node's value in each of its formats
cases.about: F19, Save Result as a basic feature of the engine SDKs (the maintainer, 2026-11-22: 'Make the save an basic feature'). The test engine's result node lists its own formats (`save_formats`: its Quoted Text, then the SDK's Text). Once it has run, its face and its menu offer Save Result…; invoked, the core asks where (file.save, the node's formats as the kinds, its first's extension on the suggested name) and, for a format with options, asks for them with its form (Quoted Text's mark); the engine writes each file (spec 15). The bytes are read back by the engine's own Read Text File node. The menu item's command run as it is (`command.run run.save {…, ask: true}`) asks the same, as does a tap on the footer's Save Result… line, a core gesture in every shell (`footer`: a shell that measures its footer's lines; cancelled here). `saves`: the driver's shell can write the case's $scratch folder

cases.name: ports: saving an array that isn't shaped like a picture as PNG asks first
cases.about: Decisions 2A and 3A (2026-11-22): the test engine's result Strip is a 4 by 1000 array. Save Result… to a .png file is a person's save (`question`), so the engine answers with a question instead of writing, and the core asks its prompt (kind saveShape: Save as PNG anyway, Save as NumPy (.npy), Cancel, the shape in its detail). NumPy writes the .npy file beside the name chosen; asked again, PNG anyway writes the picture; a script's run.save with an explicit path is never asked. `saves`: the driver's shell can write the case's $scratch folder

cases.name: ports: a path input's Browse asks for a file by its hints, and the answer sets the value
cases.about: B133 (2026-11-23, the maintainer: "Yes, fix b133 on all systems"): a path row (the test engine's Read Text File, a file it opens, filtered to Text .txt) has a Browse button at the right end of its field (geometry::browse_rect); a tap there is the core's row.browse, which asks file.open with purpose path, the hint's filters as kinds and the hint itself, and closes a field editor open on a row first. The answer is set as typing sets it: one undo step (Set Value). row.browse is invoked from ui.invoke and command.run as well (an ask first). Where the shell measures its rows, the tap itself is checked

cases.name: ports: a value with a recipe offers Recipe, and one without doesn't
cases.about: Decision 7A (2026-11-22): recipes stay with engines that track lineage. The test engine's Traced node sends its text with a recipe (`Display.recipe`), so its pop-out says hasRecipe and viewer.recipe gives the recipe; the Result node's pop-out has none, and viewer.recipe answers null. The shells' Recipe button follows hasRecipe

cases.name: a run's state arrives in the scene
cases.about: run.start, then ui.waitRun; each face's run state reads done (or cached) in scene.get, and ui.inspect's run is idle

cases.name: a watched text value arrives as text.plain, and a scalar as scalar
cases.about: run.watch of an output runs what it needs; ui.inspect's watched names the value, its media and its viewer (text.plain, scalar), with the text's excerpt and a scalar's value inline

cases.name: a watched picture arrives as picture
cases.about: an encoded image watched: ui.inspect's watched has media image, viewer picture and its rgba8 rendition; media.get decodes it where the shell serves it

cases.name: hostile gestures and queries are refused, and the core still serves
cases.about: the hostile-input sweep for what a shell sends in N2 and N3: ui.gesture, geometry.*, scene.get, theme.get, palette.*, canvas.palette's wire, edit.move, selection.nudge

cases.name: a value typed into a row is checked, held to its range, and is one undo step
cases.about: N4 slice 2: a tap on a row that can be edited opens the core's field editor (row.edit, the scene's view.edit); row.set parses what the field holds, holds a number to its range with a note, refuses what isn't a number and changes nothing, and is one undo step (Set Value) that undo and redo take back and forth; the same value again is no step; Escape (row.edit open: false) closes it

expect./result/note: count is at most 10: set to 10

cases.name: every widget kind is set through its row, and a value that isn't one of its choices is refused
cases.about: N4 slice 2: row.set for a text, a whole and a fractional number, a switch, a choice, several choices, several lines and a colour (sent as [r, g, b] and stored in the port's #rrggbb); a choice that isn't one is refused and changes nothing

cases.name: a tap flips a switch and a drag on a number scrubs it, each one undo step
cases.about: N4 slice 2: the core decides that a tap on a switch's row is row.set to the other state, and that a drag beginning on a number's row is a scrub (kind 8 on the C ABI): its moves carry the value (a screen point at a time, at the zoom the begin gave; amount moves 0.01 a point) and change nothing; its end is one row.set; a cancelled scrub sets nothing

cases.name: the more-button opens the node's menu
cases.about: N4 slice 2: a tap on a face's more-button (the part menu the shell measured) runs no command and replies with the node's context and its menu, as a context gesture does

cases.name: a wire running right to left is routed round its faces, and hit there
cases.about: N4 slice 2 (the maintainer, N3 exit card 13): a plain wire whose input is left of its output leaves to the right, runs along a channel clear of both faces and comes into its input from the left: nine cubics (28 points) instead of the four of a wire left to right; the hit test follows that shape

cases.name: faces that overlap are shown apart, and the graph keeps its positions
cases.about: N4 slice 2 (decision 13): where two measured faces overlap (a face grown after a run, or placed over another), the scene shows the later one out of the way, below or to the right with a gap; the push is the view's: graph.get's positions, the undo step and the dirty state are as they were

cases.name: the parameters inspector lists every input, and a hidden one is set, shown and reset
cases.about: N4 slice 3: node.parameters opens the inspector (the scene's view.windows.parameters); parameters.get lists every input, shown on the face or not; node.face hides an input from the face (a view change, no undo step) and shows it again; row.set sets a hidden input, one undo step, and reset: true puts the default back; node.parameters {} closes it

cases.name: a group is made, entered and edited inside, left, ungrouped, and undone
cases.about: N4 slice 3: group.create from a selection, canvas.focus enters it (only its members are shown, the breadcrumb is in the scene's focus.path), a member renamed in place inside it (name.edit, name.set), the group renamed in place, left (canvas.focus null), collapsed and expanded, ungrouped, and Ungroup undone

cases.name: a frame is made round a selection, renamed in place, resized, and grows with a member pushed out of another's way
cases.about: N4 slice 3: frame.add round the selection, name.edit on its tab and name.set (one undo step), frame.resize; two faces placed one over the other are shown apart (12.11), and the frame that holds them is shown grown to hold the one pushed, while the graph keeps its size

cases.name: a net is made, joined, renamed in place and left
cases.about: N4 slice 3: wire.label draws a wire as a net (its driver's tag says how many inputs it feeds), net.connect joins another input to it, name.edit and name.set rename it in place, wire.unlabel takes one input back out as a wire, and undo puts it back; every step but the rename's opening is one undo step

cases.name: a value popped out is a window of the core's: brought forward, viewed and closed
cases.about: N4 slice 3 (the Watched column gone, the maintainer: 'Eliminate the side column in favor of just the popout window'): a double tap on an output pin pops its value out (view.popout), the scene's view.windows lists it with its title; asking again brings it forward (raised); popout.get reads its value and the viewer's state, which viewer.text and viewer.zoom change; view.close closes it

cases.name: Select mode and Share are the core's commands, and the toolbar's state is the core's
cases.about: N4 slice 3 (golden rule 4, the maintainer: 'No exceptions to the rule'): canvas.selectMode toggles the core's Select mode (the scene's view.select, View › Select Mode's check); graph.share is File › Share…, disabled with the reason until the graph has a file (or, in a shell that declares no share sheet, the egui editor since 2026-11-21, with the core's 'Sharing isn't available in this editor'); menu.get's toolbar context gives every toolbar button with its label, icon, enabled state and check from the core

$one: save the graph first: Share sends its file
Sharing isn't available in this editor

cases.name: settings are the core's: a setting set is read back, kept, and reset
cases.about: N4 slice 4: settings.get is the model a shell renders (sections, items, kinds, values, the command each is set through); view.animationSpeed and theme.setToken change it, it is read back, and on a shell whose core keeps a preferences file (prefs) what that file holds now has it (what a reopen reads); then both are reset

cases.name: a theme chosen is the scene's, and Match the System is one of the built-in themes
cases.about: N4 slice 4: view.theme changes the theme every scene is built in; theme.get says which and has every token the scene names; system shows Paper or Dusk by the system's appearance; back to Paper, then Match the System again (the default), so a shell's kept preferences are left as they were

cases.name: an autosaved document saves itself once a change settles, and a failure is reported
cases.about: N4 slice 4 (contract 4.4): document.autosave turns autosave on with a file in the core's scratch folder; a frame added is on disk once it settles (the file read back matches the graph, the document clean); a file that can't be written is reported failed with its reason and the document stays dirty; then off

cases.name: the control port asks for its token, whatever address it listens on
cases.about: N4 slice 4: a driver over the control port (on a device, the local network's) opens a second connection and is refused with a wrong token, and a request sent before authenticating is refused too; the connection the suite runs on authenticated with the pre-shared token

cases.name: a number shows the same text everywhere: an INT whole, a FLOAT at the decimals its port gives
cases.about: N4 slice 4 (the maintainer: "precision should be set to something sensible"): a FLOAT set to a slider's 0.30000000000000004 shows 0.30 (its port's two decimals, not the float's noise) in the parameters inspector and on the face, and an INT set to 6.7 is 7 and shows 7, never decimals; the scene and parameters.get carry the text so every shell shows the same

cases.name: a table popped out by a person is sorted and paged by the core
cases.about: N4 slice 5: a TABLE value popped out by a double tap on its pin opens table.grid; viewer.data reads its rows on the media workers, typed columns with the core's number text; viewer.table sorts it (the order the core's) and pages it, and popout.get reads the state back; value.copy gives it as tab-separated text

cases.name: a JSON value popped out by a person is an outline the core opens and closes
cases.about: N4 slice 5: a JSON value popped out shows as YAML first (the maintainer: 'format as Yaml for display'); the Tree viewer is offered beside it; viewer.tree opens and closes members by JSON pointer, closing one closes what is inside it, and viewer.data lists each open member's children; value.copy copies a member

cases.name: a sound popped out by a person plays, pauses and seeks through the core, with its waveform and spectrogram
cases.about: N4 slice 5: an AUDIO value (Array to Audio) popped out opens the audio viewer; viewer.audio plays, seeks, loops and sets the level, the state the core's (popout.get), seq rising with each start or seek; the waveform and spectrogram are made from the full samples on the media workers (media.get waveform, spectrogram), never on a shell's thread. B56 (decision 15): the loop is set before play, so a shell that reports a sound's end (its player, or a muted clock, reaching the end tells the core, which raises seq) never does during the case, however long its steps take: the 64 ms sound no longer has to outlast two steps

cases.name: an array popped out by a person is a picture, and its numbers a grid paged by the core
cases.about: N4 slice 5: an ARRAY popped out shows as pictures first, its values a viewer away (array.grid): viewer.data reads a page of its numbers as the core's text, from the array's own bytes; viewer.grid pages it; the shape and dtype come with it

cases.name: an array's view is chosen through the core and its pictures change
cases.about: B154 slice 1 (floor F51, view modes): an ARRAY popped out offers its wire type's views (auto, color, stretch, clip, heat, labels, angle) in popout.get's viewModes, with the one shown in viewMode; run.view {popout, view} shows another and a run (cached) brings its pictures, which differ; an unknown view is refused; each channel's statistics carry its NaN count and its 256-bin histogram, whose heights follow viewer.array {log}

cases.name: a zoom asked of a pop-out reaches its shell once, with where to centre
cases.about: B159: viewer.zoom {popout, to?, at?} on a pop-out is in popout.get's zoomAsk {seq, to, at}, seq rising with each ask, so a native shell (which keeps its picture's zoom and view itself) applies each once: to is fit, 1:1, in, out or screen pixels per value pixel, at the value pixel to centre; nothing asked, null

cases.name: a wide array's numbers are shown 64 columns at a time, in the core's window
cases.about: Decision 26 (N4 person gate, the maintainer: 'Move it into the core'): which columns of a wide array the numbers grid shows is the core's viewer state, not each shell's. viewer.grid {cols: next | prev | first | last} steps the window by 64 columns and {col} shows the window holding a column; it never starts past the last window; viewer.data's grid page reads the window (firstCol, endCol, colsShown, prevCols, nextCols) and takes no column of its own; popout.get's state has it; junk is refused and changes nothing

cases.name: a picture popped out by a person shows a channel, reads its own numbers and asks for detail
cases.about: N4 slice 5: an IMAGE popped out: viewer.picture shows one channel (the state the core's), viewer.data's probe reads the picture file's own numbers at a pixel (never the 8-bit picture's), and a zoom past its pixels asks for detail (viewer.zoom detail); the picture file decodes larger on the media workers (media.get image)

cases.name: an SVG popped out by a person is drawn, with its source a viewer away
cases.about: N4 slice 5: an SVG popped out shows as svg (drawn on the media workers at the size asked, media.get svg), with its source offered as text (text.plain, 'Source')

cases.name: a value read as what it isn't is refused with a reason, and the core still serves
cases.about: N4 slice 5: a text value asked for as a table, as an outline of bytes, or with junk parameters: viewer.data says why (status failed, or the request refused), never crashes, and the pop-out and the core go on; the viewer commands refuse what isn't theirs

cases.name: the Messages window is the core's: opened, read and closed
cases.about: N4 slice 5: view.messages opens the Messages window in the scene's view.windows (messages: true); messages.get gives the status bar's messages in full (a failed node's error first, with its node); view.messages {open: false} closes it

cases.name: the Cache Report and the graph's Parameters window are the core's: opened, read, edited and closed
cases.about: N4 slice 6: run.cacheReport and view.params open windows in the scene's view.windows (cache, params, with a reports stamp); report.get gives each as sections of rows, the Parameters window's name and description as fields their commands take; a rename through the field's command is read back; closing them by their commands leaves no window

cases.name: windows opened as another closes stay open: the shell never closes what the core opened
cases.about: N4 device gate, B43: on the iPad a sheet presented over one whose dismissal hadn't run went with it, and the shell then told the core the window was closed (the graph's Parameters window, seen on a device). The Messages window opened and closed, then the Cache Report and Parameters opened at once, three times: both must stay open (holds, for a second), and close by their commands

cases.name: Compare pins two values popped out by a person, side by side or split, and unpins them
cases.about: N4 slice 6: a value popped out by a double tap is pinned as A with viewer.pin {slot, popout} (the Apple apps have no Watched panel), another as B; the scene's view.windows has compare; compare.get gives both sides as popout.get has a value; viewer.compare changes how; viewer.unpin forgets them and Compare closes

cases.name: Zoom In, Zoom Out and Actual Size are the core's commands
cases.about: N5 slice 3 (golden rule 4, the maintainer: 'No exceptions to the rule'): the zoom keys are canvas.zoom, by a factor or to a zoom; the view stays the shell's, and the scene's view.zoom asks it once per seq; neither both nor none is taken, and nothing in the graph changes

cases.name: Install Engine… is offered as the platform allows, by the core
cases.about: B71 (the maintainer, 2026-11-21: 'Install engine is greyed out, no engines available. WTF?'): whether engine.install is enabled is the core's, decided by the platform's declared capabilities (subprocess and python), never by which shell runs; engine.list, ui.inspect's engine and the Engine menu's Install Engine… agree, and a disabled one says why; Cancel Install is disabled with nothing installing

cases.name: Install Engine…'s form offers the public engines as a pick list, with any other repository typed
cases.about: Decision 5 (N4 person gate, the maintainer: 'Add the pick-list field kind'): the form the core asks Install Engine… with has its repository as a pick field (kind pick, the public engines as choices, other: true), drawn by every shell as a pop-up or combo box beside its label with a line of text for any other; the list is the core's alone. Run where the platform can install and the core asks with its form (`install`); cancelling the ask installs nothing

cases.name: an engine a manifest in the engines folder names is offered, and Reload Engine List keeps it
cases.about: B71: the native apps read no engine manifests, so an engine installed with the egui editor was never offered there. A driver with `manifests` has the suite's engines folder (fixtures/conformance/engines: probe.toml, an engine running elsewhere, so every platform lists it): engine.list's choices and the Engine menu offer it, and engine.manifests.reload reads the folder again and still offers it. docs/interface.md 16.6: a driver that also has `copied_manifest` has instead the folder conformance::copied_manifest_folder makes in scratch (probe.toml, and copied.toml, a copy of a project's manifest away from its project); its steps check that engine.list's and ui.inspect's choices carry the warning for that engine and not for the probe, and that the Engine menu's items for it carry it as `warning`, still enabled, their hover starting with it

cases.name: a value with an editor promoted to a group opens the member's editor from the group's face
cases.about: FR1 (the maintainer, 2026-11-23: a row that opens it, for every value an engine names an editor for): the test engine's Curve names an editor no application registers, so every shell shows the member's short form; promoted by the same command and menu as any input, on the collapsed group's face it is a row whose tap opens the member's editor (node.editor), here the core's value window

cases.name: the curves editor's commands edit an array node's curves, one undo step each, and a run sends the editor its data
cases.about: S4a (the maintainer, 2026-11-23: a general curve editor in the shell, every edit a core command; docs/shell-interface.md 12.21): the array engine's Apply Curve names the curves editor on its curves input; node.editorData says so before a run (no data), curves.edit and curves.preset are an undo step each, and after a run the editor's data holds the channel's histogram and the picture, so Equalize works

cases.name: the mask editor's strokes are files, one undo step each, and a graph with nowhere to write asks for a folder once
cases.about: S4b (the maintainer, 2026-11-23: decisions 1A, 3A, 4A, 7A): the array engine's Paint Mask names the mask editor on its edit input; after a run node.editorData has the picture at the mask's size. A person's stroke (ui.invoke) on a graph with no file asks for a folder (folder.pick, purpose edits); the answer is kept (mask.folder, one undo step) and the stroke goes there as a new file (mask.stroke, one undo step); each stroke is a new file and one undo takes one back; Clear drops the edit. `saves`: the driver's shell can write the case's $scratch folder

cases.name: Clean Up Mask Files removes the mask files nothing reaches, after asking a person first
cases.about: S4b (the maintainer, 2026-11-23: decision 5B, "Ref commonkit -- both"; commonkit 0.3's prune_folder): a graph saved in the case's scratch folder, two strokes, saved, and opened again so the undo history is fresh: the first stroke's file is then reached by nothing (not the graph, not undo or redo, not the saved graph beside it). mask.prune lists it in a dry run (the default) and removes nothing; a person's Clean Up Mask Files (ui.invoke) asks first with the count (prompt pruneMasks), and Remove takes it and its sidecar; the graph's own file stays. age_s 0 stands in for the day a file must age. `saves`: the driver's shell can write the case's $scratch folder

cases.name: a new graph is saved as .plum, and a .json graph opens and saves back to its .json
cases.about: FR2 (the maintainer: the default graph file extension .json -> .plum, .json still accepted). graph.fileTypes is the one rule every shell reads; Save of a new graph and Save As offer the graph's stem with .plum, .plum first and .json still a kind; Open offers both; a graph opened from a .json file saves to it with no ask; both open, read by content. `saves`: the driver's shell can write the case's $scratch folder
